description: Cross-language vector for signature fields carried on the wrong act type (Section 7.3.1). Each act type has its own signature field, and a receiver refuses an act that carries a signature field belonging to another act type, whatever its value, null included: a verifier reads any such field as a signature claim (Section 9A.6), so admitting the act would let one message leave the session with an evidence record that fails verification or cannot be generated at all. Both suites build the session below, send each case's act through the state machine, and must reach its verdict, error code and error message. They then close the session, if it is still open, with an signed withdrawal from the initiator, generate the initiator's evidence record, and require it to verify: a refused act never enters the record, and each signed control shows the same act without the stray field records cleanly. An unsigned decline is refused whether or not it carries a stray field, because a party's own decline must be signed (Sections 7.5, 7.6). Keys are generated by each suite and are not part of the vector.

act_setup.offer: A fresh session. The act is the initiator's round-1 offer at sequence_number 1, signed in protocol_act_signature.
act_setup.counteroffer: The initiator's signed round-1 offer at sequence_number 1 has been processed. The act is the responder's round-2 counteroffer at sequence_number 2, signed in protocol_act_signature.
act_setup.acceptance: The initiator's signed round-1 offer at sequence_number 1 has been processed. The act is the responder's acceptance of it at sequence_number 2, signed in acceptance_signature.
act_setup.rejection: The initiator's signed round-1 offer at sequence_number 1 has been processed. The act is the responder's rejection of it at round_number 1 and sequence_number 2, reason_code PRICE_TOO_HIGH; when signed is true it is signed in rejection_signature, and when false it carries no sender_verification_method and no signature.
act_setup.withdrawal: The initiator's signed round-1 offer at sequence_number 1 has been processed. The act is the responder's withdrawal at round_number 1 and sequence_number 2, reason_code STRATEGY_DECISION; when signed is true it is signed in withdrawal_signature, and when false it carries no sender_verification_method and no signature.

cases_description: Each case builds its act_type's act as act_setup says, signed in its own field when signed is true, and then, when the case names a stray_field, sets that field to stray_value. The own signature is made before the stray field is added; the stray field is outside every signed scope, so it does not change what the own signature covers.
